# Storyboard — The ferment log

## Waiting on Ines

1. Contact address and workshop booking details; apprentice path is an enquiry, not a claim of vacancies.
2. Own pot/larder photos, one redacted ferment-log excerpt and a prep-list excerpt. No manufactured values or tasks.
3. Restaurant permission before any Priya photo, credit always; Olu permission before any drawing or scan containing it. Neither needed for this direction.

Concept chosen by assistant under user's judgement instruction. This is a complete planning proposal; storyboard not yet accepted. No site built. All screen quantities are design estimates, not rigid scroll locks. No finished captions here; beats identify facts for later copy.

## Governing idea

Question: What happens before the menu is written?

One log, eight leaves, five-to-six chapters. Confirmed log fields carry the order. A final menu chapter answers using the user's menu-written-last statement. The log itself represents current practice. Opening pot photo names a stated influence without inventing an origin story. The paper format is a design assumption, not a description of her actual log medium.

## Chapters

| Chapter | Name in form | Role | Content | Same eight leaves | Interaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Started | Opening, who, origin | Name, Leeds, Head Chef since Sep 2022; question; grandmother's pot | Bound log opens, inner face shows owned pot photo | Skip to contact; chapter navigation; photo details |
| 2 | Salt | How | Start date, salt, check days, ready date; prep list | Leaves fan; a real excerpt is front-facing | Open readable HTML transcript |
| 3 | Checks | Work, where from | Actual record/check evidence; ten-week unpaid stage, washing/labels/two garum batches | Same leaves form parallel record rows; two leaves stand as a modest stage note | Inspect owned larder photo; transcript; no simulated ticking |
| 4 | Ready | Outcomes | Whole-kitchen waste measure and definition | Two leaves become paired evidence panels, others remain visible | Expand measurement scope |
| 5 | Log note | What others say | Exact approved Callum quote; distinguish opinion from measurement | One leaf turns front-on, remaining seven collect behind it | Accessible quote, attribution |
| 6 | Closed log / Menu | Answer, reach | Menu last; apprentice, writer and workshop contact paths | Eight leaves close into original whole | Three labelled enquiry actions |

Log note and close are editorial additions, not fabricated fields in the working record. A source-only career chronology is not included. Brine and Sunday Pot are optional future additions after roles/rights are confirmed; no empty project cards.

## Beats

Each row is one settled scene and one corresponding ordinary HTML text block. No scene requires dragging. On desktop a single sticky scene transforms between states; leave text readable during transitions.

| Chapter / beat | Screens | Arrangement | Faces | Added elements | Caption basis / working title |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Started / 1 | 1 | Eight leaves bound; cover opens slightly | Ines name/role/location and question on cover; own grandmother-pot photo on first leaf | Persistent chapter rail and contact jump | Identity from profile; title corrected by user; question editorial |
| Started / 2 | 0.5 | Pot leaf tilts front-on, seven remain visibly bound | Own pot image, factual identification; current-role record | Small HTML evidence preview links to Ready | Influence stated in notes; ownership confirmed; no specific lesson |
| Salt / 1 | 1 | Eight leaves fan; one excerpt front-on | Authentic redacted log excerpt; actual field names | Field highlights in adjacent HTML, no invented entries | User's start date/salt/check days/ready description |
| Salt / 2 | 0.75 | Two central leaves side by side, six visible at edges | Actual prep excerpt and log excerpt | Simple connecting rule, not a recipe/process diagram | Confirmed daily documents and menu-last practice |
| Checks / 1 | 1 | Leaves arranged in readable parallel rows | Selected real record and own larder image; other faces carry crops of those same verified sources | Only actual record checks represented | Real excerpt pending; no fictional cadence or readiness |
| Checks / 2 | 0.75 | Two leaves advance; six keep context | Fjaerland stage facts in plain type, no lab imagery | None | Ten weeks, unpaid; washing/labels, helped with two batches; no researcher wording |
| Ready / 1 | 1 | Two leaves as adjacent panels; six collect behind | 14 kg/week and 5 kg/week, “we” attribution; scope alongside | No causal arrows or fabricated time chart | Confirmed whole kitchen; prep/plate; one month 2023; bones excluded/stock |
| Log note / 1 | 0.75 | One front-on leaf, seven behind | Callum's exact sourced quote, name/title | None | User confirms quote permission; opinion, not measured result |
| Closed log / 1 | 1 | All eight reunite as closed log; question face returns | Menu-written-last fact; factual chapter index | Three HTML enquiry destinations | User's workflow and audiences; no job-seeking or fictional openings |

Estimated desktop story: about 8.5 viewports, shorter with modest copy. Scroll is native, reversible, never trapped; transformations follow scroll without forcing a pause. Real images/text are not replaced by decorative filler if assets are missing: hold those faces as requirements in the plan and use confirmed fields in text in any subsequent draft.

## Thirty-second visit

First screen: name, role/location, question and glimpse of owned pot photo. A compact evidence preview states the scope of the confirmed kitchen waste result and links to Ready. It remains explicitly team evidence. Persistent Contact link jumps to all three audience routes; navigation jumps to each chapter. Workshop visitors can go directly to booking information without completing the story.

## Without the scene

| Where | Experience |
|---|---|
| Phone | Single-column text and static/briefly transitioning page crops; no tall pinned sequence. Object appears as a compact log illustration in each chapter. Full-size accessible image/transcript when selected. Navigation in an expandable labelled menu; visible contact link. Native vertical scroll; no hover-only content. |
| Reduced motion | Static arrangements per chapter, no parallax, page flips, scroll easing or camera travel. Same text, images and actions. Respect system preference and offer a persistent motion toggle. |
| No WebGL | Pre-rendered/static log states plus ordinary text/image narrative; identical links and evidence. |
| No JavaScript | Server-rendered/static HTML chapters, figures, transcripts and anchor links; contact links work. No hidden reveal-dependent text. |

Browser zoom and keyboard navigation preserve reading order. Main text is never a 3D texture. Selected labels/images have accessible HTML counterparts. Motion toggling cannot reset reading position. Focus outlines, semantic headings, alt text and at least WCAG AA contrast are launch requirements.

## Look and type

Chosen: paper and ink, drawn from the proposed log material and label photographs. Photo colours come from actual assets, not invented jar contents. Matte paper edges, restrained thickness and gentle daylight; avoid glossy glass and ambient particle effects.

| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Pieces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper and ink — chosen | Warm paper #F3EFE5 | Charcoal #242820 | Deep olive #46543A | Off-white paper, muted ink rules, real image crops |
| White label — alternative | #FAF9F5 | #202622 | Dark teal #285950 | Pale label paper, fine grey rules |
| Evening log — alternative | #202722 | #F3EFE5 | Pale ochre #D2B575 | Warm paper leaves against dark ground |

These are alternatives, not three skins to implement. Keep palette restrained and verify actual interactive/secondary-text contrast. Accent marks fields, selected chapter and focus; never the only way to convey status.

Typography: Source Serif 4 for narrative/headings; IBM Plex Mono for log fields, dates and small navigation labels. Two families, locally hosted open-license subsets. Body about 18–20 px desktop, 17–18 px phone; line length 55–65 characters. Strong readable hierarchy; no oversized word that crowds out identity/evidence/actions. Preserve actual handwriting only in source images, with transcripts; do not manufacture handwriting in her voice.

## Everything else

“Build” below means in scope for a future implementation, not authorization to build now.

| Requirement | Build / later / never | Decider / specifics |
|---|---|---|
| Way around page | Build | Assistant: chapter anchors, contact skip, keyboard and touch access |
| A page per project | Later | Assistant: only when verified material warrants a real case study |
| Every project listed | Later | Assistant: no unverified Brine/Sunday Pot claims or padding |
| Contact and CV | Build contact; never job-search CV in this scope | User audience; assistant chooses three enquiry routes pending destinations |
| Testimonials | Build | User approved Callum; show exact quote with attribution |
| Languages | Build English; later additional language | Assistant: no language proficiency inferred |
| Shared link/icon | Build | Assistant: factual name/role description, log-page thumbnail, simple ruled-page icon; cleared image only |
| Missing address page | Build | Assistant: plain 404, home/contact links |
| Blog | Later | Assistant: only if Ines wants an ongoing writing workflow |
| Chat | Never in this scope | Assistant: adds burden without serving stated audiences |
| Legal/privacy notice | Build as applicable | Assistant: accurate site/operator/contact/data handling info; hosting/form choices determine requirements |
| Workshop booking | Build link initially | Assistant: existing destination if supplied, otherwise workshop enquiry; no invented dates or payment flow |
| Apprentice enquiry | Build | Assistant: specific route; no vacancy/intake promise |
| Writer contact | Build | Assistant: contact and factual short bio; downloadable assets later with rights/credits |
| Content updates | Build simple documented process | Assistant: workshop destination and images/credits editable separately from scene code; no CMS assumed |
| Search/accessibility/performance | Build | Assistant: semantic indexed HTML, metadata, canonical URL once known, sitemap, 404, keyboard/zoom/device checks |
| Analytics/cookies | Later | Assistant: no tracking by default; revisit if a concrete measurement need arises |

## Motion, performance and future validation

One scene and the same eight leaves throughout. Lazy-load optional 3D after useful HTML renders; pause rendering when offscreen, tab hidden or scene settled. Avoid heavy physics, real-time refraction and continuously moving light. Images responsive/compressed, font subsets and lightweight geometry. Phone defaults to simpler presentation; load scene only where it can run smoothly.

Future acceptance: reading/contact work with no JS and no WebGL; reduced-motion has no camera/page travel; all links/controls work by keyboard/touch; text survives 200% zoom; no scroll traps; correct team attribution/time/scope beside waste figures; Fjaerland never framed as research; excluded prices/faces absent; credits and approvals complete. Test a modest phone and desktop; target Core Web Vitals LCP <=2.5 s, INP <=200 ms, CLS <=0.1. These are targets, not measured results.

## Assumptions and review

Assistant chose concept A, light palette, typography, six-chapter order, eight-leaf visual representation, mobile simplification, English and direct enquiry routes. Paper log is a design metaphor; exact log format is unknown. Nothing about recipes, workshop topics, vacancies, ongoing waste performance or unconfirmed achievements assumed.

Ask Ines to accept storyboard or name changes. Caption writing and building remain outside this planning version. No acceptance has yet been recorded.
# Planning handover

## Authorized scope

Distinctive personal portfolio planning only. No implementation, publishing or costs. User provided fact corrections and authorized judgement on uncovered matters, with stated assumptions.

## Exists

- facts.md: original source reading plus user corrections; unanswered facts stay unresolved.
- concepts.md: three concepts; assistant selected A, the ferment log, under judgement instruction.
- storyboard.md: complete six-chapter proposal, per-beat screen/scene/content specifications, visual alternatives and chosen palette/type, mobile/accessibility/fallback requirements, site scope and future validation targets. No finished captions.
- decided-for-you.md: choices, reasons and how to change them.

## Confirmed essentials

Head Chef since September 2022; acting since March. Norway was ten-week unpaid stage, no research. Waste is whole-kitchen prep/plate, weighed over one month in 2023, 14 to 5 kg/week, “we”, excludes bones. Log fields and menu-last practice confirmed. Audience apprentices/writers/workshop bookers, not employers. Own phone/pot images; approved Callum quote. No supplier prices or staff faces without consent. Priya credit required; restaurant reuse approval pending. Olu approval pending.

## Next

Await user's yes to storyboard or changes. Contact/booking destinations, own image files and authentic redacted excerpts still needed. Third-party images not needed to support chosen direction. Do not interpret judgement authorization as factual confirmation or rights clearance.

When storyboard accepted, record acceptance and finalize this handover. Building is not part of this skill version; any later implementation would be a separately authorized task. No website or preview exists.

item.text:
The site will be **one continuous ferment log**, answering: **“What happens before the menu is written?”** It follows your records and working practice, then ends with the menu and clear routes for apprentices, workshop visitors and food writers.

The complete specification is saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-pLveBf/docs/story/storyboard.md). Your recommended direction is recorded as selected. **Nothing has been built.**

Before any future implementation, these remain needed:

1. Your contact address and workshop booking destination/details.
2. Selected own photographs and authentic, redacted ferment-log and prep-list excerpts.
3. Restaurant permission if Priya’s photos are included, with her credit; Olu’s permission before showing his drawings or scans containing them. The chosen concept can work without either.

**The central object and page structure**

Eight paper leaves form one bound log. The same leaves remain present from the first screen to the last: they open, fan out, arrange into records, display evidence and close again.

The paper format is a visual interpretation of your log, not a claim about its actual medium. Its faces carry your photographs, real records and confirmed facts. The narrative remains ordinary readable text alongside the scene.

On desktop, the log occupies a sticky area while the text scrolls beside it. The whole story takes roughly eight screen heights, adjusted to the actual content. Scrolling stays native and reversible; visitors can jump straight to a chapter or contact.

**1. Started — meet you and establish the question**

The first screen shows your name, Leeds, your Head Chef role at Saltmarsh, and the central question. The role uses **September 2022**; acting Head Chef from March can appear in the supporting detail.

The log begins closed, then opens enough to reveal your photograph of your grandmother’s ogiri pot. The image identifies a stated influence. It does not invent a childhood scene, a lesson she taught you, or a connection between that pot and a restaurant recipe.

A compact evidence preview links to the later whole-kitchen waste result. Someone who stops here still gets your identity, work, some evidence and a way to contact you.

Visitors can click:

- A chapter menu to jump anywhere.
- **Contact** to reach the three enquiry routes.
- The evidence preview to jump to **Ready**.
- The pot photograph to expand its image details.

**2. Salt — show how the work is recorded**

The log opens into a fan. One leaf turns squarely toward the visitor, showing an authentic redacted record and its fields: **start date, salt, check days and ready date**.

A second beat brings the prep-list excerpt alongside it. This establishes the two documents you work from, while the menu remains the final destination.

The record’s actual values appear only after you supply the excerpt. No salt percentages, dates, jar names or tasks are fabricated.

Visitors can click:

- **Read the log** to expand a readable transcript.
- **Read the prep list** to expand its redacted contents.

Field highlights can connect the text to the image, but the visitor never needs to interact with the 3D to understand either document.

**3. Checks — make the practice visible**

The same leaves arrange into parallel rows. A selected real record sits beside one of your own larder photographs. Any highlighted checks come from that record; the animation does not simulate fermentation or invent a checking schedule.

A second beat brings forward a modest note about Fjaerland: a **ten-week unpaid stage**, washing and labelling jars, and helping with two batches of garum. It stays specific and proportionate, without research language or an unconfirmed career timeline.

Visitors can click:

- **View larder photograph** for a larger accessible image.
- **Read record** for its transcript.

The scene presents evidence of practice; it does not become a recipe browser or offer readiness instructions.

**4. Ready — show the measured result**

Two leaves become adjacent evidence panels showing **14 kg per week** and **5 kg per week**.

The scope stays visible beside them: **whole-kitchen prep and plate waste, weighed over one month in 2023, with “we” attribution**. Bones were excluded because they went to stock.

There is no invented monthly chart, implied ongoing performance, or animation suggesting a particular cause for the reduction.

Visitors can expand a measurement note, but the essential attribution and limitations are readable immediately.

**5. Log note — let someone else speak**

One page turns forward while the other seven gather behind it. It carries Callum’s approved words:

> “Ines turned our bins into a larder. The best thing on the menu most weeks started as something we used to throw away.”

His name and Saltmarsh-owner attribution appear alongside it. This is clearly a recommendation, separate from the measured result.

There is no testimonial carousel or additional interaction needed to read it.

**6. Menu — complete the answer and invite the next step**

The eight leaves reunite into the closed log. The ending returns to your confirmed practice: **the menu is the last thing written each week**.

Three clear actions sit beside the object:

- **Apprentice enquiry:** contact you about learning or applying, without implying current vacancies or a confirmed intake.
- **Workshop booking:** go to your supplied booking destination; use an enquiry route until those details exist.
- **Writer contact:** reach you directly, with a concise factual introduction.

The email address should also be visible as a backup. A visitor can reach this section directly from the first screen.

The footer contains contact, credits, applicable privacy/legal information and a back-to-top link.

**The look**

The visual direction comes from paper, labels and the proposed log:

| Use | Colour |
|---|---|
| Background | Warm paper **#F3EFE5** |
| Main text | Charcoal **#242820** |
| Accent | Deep olive **#46543A** |

The leaves have matte surfaces, restrained thickness, fine rules and gentle shadows. Your real photographs supply the richer colour and texture.

**Source Serif 4** carries headings and narrative. **IBM Plex Mono** carries log fields, dates and small labels. Body text stays comfortably readable, with approximately 55–65 characters per line. Actual handwriting remains in photographs or scans, accompanied by transcripts.

The olive accent marks selected chapters, links and focus states. Meaning never depends on colour alone.

**Movement and interaction**

Each transition explains a change in the content: opening introduces you, fanning reveals fields, rows expose records, paired pages compare evidence, and closing completes the answer.

The site uses one scene rather than a new effect in every section. Settled pages remain still while visitors read. There is no required dragging, scroll trapping, autoplay sound or custom cursor.

Image details and transcripts use simple inline disclosures. If a larger overlay is later necessary, it must have a visible close button, Escape support and correct keyboard-focus behaviour.

**On a phone and without 3D**

| Situation | Experience |
|---|---|
| **Phone** | Single-column narrative with compact log illustrations between sections. No long pinned sequence. Records open at readable sizes; contact stays easy to reach. |
| **Reduced motion** | Static chapter arrangements, with no page flips, parallax or camera travel. Respect the system preference and provide a motion toggle. |
| **No WebGL** | Static images of the log arrangements beside the complete narrative, records and links. |
| **No JavaScript** | Ordinary HTML chapters, figures, transcripts, disclosures and anchor links. Contact still works. |

On a phone, navigation becomes a labelled expandable menu with a visible contact link. Nothing depends on hovering.

Keyboard navigation, screen-reader structure, visible focus, descriptive image text and text at 200% zoom are part of the planned experience. Turning motion off preserves the visitor’s reading position.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Include” below means part of a future implementation, not authorization to build now.

| Item | Planned scope |
|---|---|
| Navigation | Chapter anchors, contact shortcut and keyboard skip link |
| Contact | Three audience routes using real email and supplied booking links |
| Booking | External booking destination initially; no invented dates or payment flow |
| Credits | Credits attached to displayed assets and a full credits list |
| Asset records | Owner, permission, credit, description and redaction status for every image |
| Privacy boundaries | Supplier prices and unapproved staff faces absent from public files and downloads |
| Accessibility | Semantic text, transcripts, keyboard/touch access, contrast checks and motion controls |
| Search visibility | Factual titles/descriptions, canonical address, sitemap and indexable text |
| Sharing | A log-based preview image and simple ruled-page icon using cleared material |
| Missing-page handling | A useful 404 with home and contact links |
| Privacy/legal information | Accurate information matched to the eventual hosting and data handling |
| Content updates | A documented way to change contact links, photographs, credits and workshop details |
| Hosting | Domain, HTTPS, deployment/rollback process and renewal responsibility, chosen later |
| Performance | Responsive images, local font subsets, lightweight geometry and delayed optional 3D loading |
| Validation | Modest-phone and desktop checks; keyboard, zoom, reduced-motion, no-JS and no-WebGL checks |

The initial scope is English and can be a static site with email and external booking links. A database or CMS is not assumed. Tracking is off by default.

Dedicated project pages, a blog, a press download and additional languages can follow when there is a real need and verified material. Brine and Sunday Pot remain available for later expansion once their roles and assets are settled. Chat and a job-search CV are outside this scope.

Performance targets for a future build are LCP at or below 2.5 seconds, INP at or below 200 milliseconds and CLS at or below 0.1. These are targets, not measured results.

**What I decided for you**

I chose the paper-log representation, eight leaves, six chapters, light palette, two typefaces, simpler phone presentation and three enquiry routes. These decisions are recorded in [decided-for-you.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-pLveBf/docs/story/decided-for-you.md).

The plan supplies the sequence and content subjects; finished captions remain a later editorial task grounded in the fact sheet. This completes the planning stage. Building is outside this version of the storyfolio workflow and remains explicitly unauthorised.
